methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 2 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 13 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Ephos is a Seed-stage semiconductor company that has raised €41.5M in EU funding plus $8.5M in seed capital. The Chips & Semiconductors sector includes 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers such as Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems. However, the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints to support median-based valuation.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable method here. Using total capital raised ($42M as a proxy for current valuation) and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier for progression from Seed to the next stage yields $104M. The public comparables universe shows a Semiconductors P/S median of 20.4x across three tickers, but cannot be applied without Ephos's revenue disclosure—standard practice for private-stage companies. Peer-median triangulation was not feasible due to insufficient narrow-filter matches within the same sector and stage cohort.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $88M to $119M, with a median point of $104M. This range reflects the single applicable method and carries material uncertainty given reliance on stage-based progression rather than peer or revenue-based anchoring. Key risks to this estimate include revenue trajectory, capital efficiency relative to public-market benchmarks, and the eventual comparability of this company to the fragmented semiconductor peer set as it scales.
